statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-5958: with -i and --follow-symlinks, GNU sed's open_next_file() resolves the symlink and then opens the original symlink path in a separate step, so an attacker who swaps the symlink in between can make sed read attacker-chosen content and write it to the originally resolved target (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-5958, https://bugs.debian.org/1134495, https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/05/13/1). Upstream fixed it by opening the already-resolved path (sed commit 6b9b43c55ccd3beadbc0094b983c82bdb389f33b, released in sed 4.10). Debian backported that commit to trixie in 4.9-2+deb13u1. The DHI sed package for Debian 13 is a rebuild of Debian's 4.9-2+deb13u1; the one build the DHI Debian repository publishes (amd64 and arm64), which is the fixed version used here, ships a Debian changelog that records the CVE-2026-5958 fix.
